Let $I\subset\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open time interval containing $0$. Use SI units: time is measured in seconds, spatial coordinates and lengths in metres, $\rho_0$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, $\mu$ in $\mathrm{Pa\,s}$, $u$ in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, and $p$ in $\mathrm{Pa}$. A bounded $C^1$ domain means a bounded open set locally on one side of a continuously differentiable boundary graph. The fixed spatial region $\Omega$ is either a nonempty bounded $C^1$ domain in $\mathbb R^3$ or one rectangular period cell $[0,L_1]\times[0,L_2]\times[0,L_3]$ with side lengths $L_1,L_2,L_3>0$ metres. In the bounded-domain case, let $\mathcal O\subset I\times\mathbb R^3$ be open and contain $I\times\overline\Omega$, and suppose $u\in C^2(\mathcal O,\mathbb R^3)$ and $p\in C^1(\mathcal O,\mathbb R)$. In the periodic case, take $u$ and $p$ on $I\times\mathbb R^3$, periodic with their derivatives on opposite faces of the stated cell. In either case suppose the smooth fields satisfy on the stated spacetime domain the pointwise constant-density incompressible Newtonian model equations
$$ \rho=\rho_0>0,\qquad \operatorname{div}u=0,\qquad \sigma=-pI_3+2\mu D,\qquad \rho_0D_tu=\operatorname{div}\sigma, $$
where $\mu\ge0$ is constant, the body force is zero, $D=(\nabla u+\nabla u^T)/2$, $D_tu=\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u$, and $\operatorname{div}\sigma$ is the rowwise divergence. In the bounded-domain case impose the no-slip condition $u=0$ on $I\times\partial\Omega$; in the periodic case the model equations hold on the periodic lift to $\mathbb R^3$.

For $D=(\nabla u+\nabla u^T)/2$, let $E_k(t)=\frac{\rho_0}{2}\int_\Omega |u(t,x)|^2\,dx$, using one period cell in the periodic case. For every $t_1<t_2$ in $I$,
$$ E_k(t_2)+2\mu\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\int_\Omega |D(t,x)|^2\,dx\,dt=E_k(t_1). $$
Thus $E_k$ is nonincreasing; strict decay is not claimed when $D$ vanishes. The theorem is conditional on an actual smooth solution and supplies no existence or long-time regularity result.

Proof.before:
1.1 The pointwise model equation in [A1] holds on the same fixed spatial region used in the energy integral (or on its periodic lift). Dot $\rho_0D_tu=\operatorname{div}\sigma$ with $u$. The component product rule gives $u_i\partial_{x_j}\sigma_{ij}=\partial_{x_j}(\sigma_{ij}u_i)-\sigma_{ij}\partial_{x_j}u_i$, while $D_t(|u|^2/2)=u\cdot D_tu$. Since $\rho_0$ is constant and $\operatorname{div}u=0$, this yields
$$ \partial_t\left(\frac{\rho_0|u|^2}{2}\right) +\operatorname{div}\left(\frac{\rho_0|u|^2}{2}u-\sigma^Tu\right) =-\sigma:\nabla u. $$
[A1, A2, algebra]

2.1 Integrate over the fixed domain or one periodic cell. On a no-slip boundary both flux terms vanish because $u=0$. On a periodic cell the fluxes on opposite faces cancel because their outward normals are opposite and the fields are periodic. Therefore $\frac{d}{dt}E_k(t)=-\int_\Omega\sigma:\nabla u\,dx$. [A2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Write $\nabla u=D+W$, where $W=(\nabla u-\nabla u^T)/2$ is skew-symmetric. A symmetric matrix is Frobenius-orthogonal to a skew-symmetric matrix, so $D:W=0$. The stress law gives $\sigma:\nabla u=(-pI_3+2\mu D):(D+W)=-p\,\operatorname{div}u+2\mu|D|^2=2\mu|D|^2$. Thus $\frac{d}{dt}E_k=-2\mu\int_\Omega|D|^2\,dx$. Integrating this identity from $t_1$ to $t_2$ proves the stated energy equality and nonincrease because $\mu\ge0$. [A1, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

Assume Countable Choice, meaning every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function. Let $T>0$ seconds. The spatial domain is either (B) a bounded connected nonempty open $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ with $C^2$ boundary, or (P) a periodic channel $\Omega_{L_x,h,L_z}:=(\mathbb R/L_x\mathbb Z)\times(0,h)\times(\mathbb R/L_z\mathbb Z)$ with $L_x,L_z,h>0$ metres. In (P), fields are periodic in the first and third coordinates on the Euclidean covering space, and the only physical wall boundary is $\Gamma=(\mathbb R/L_x\mathbb Z)\times\{0,h\}\times(\mathbb R/L_z\mathbb Z)$; identified periodic faces are not walls. In (B), set $\Gamma:=\partial\Omega$. In either case let $n$ be the outward unit normal on $\Gamma$, let $dx$ be Euclidean volume measure (or its periodic-cell quotient measure), and let $dS$ be the induced area measure on $\Gamma$. Let the constant mass density be $\rho>0$ kilograms per cubic metre, the constant dynamic viscosity be $\eta>0$ pascal-seconds, the body-acceleration field be $b\in C([0,T]\times\overline\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ in metres per second squared, the velocity be $u\in C^1([0,T];C^2(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R^3))$ in metres per second, and the pressure be $p\in C([0,T];C^1(\overline\Omega))$ in pascals. Define $D(u)_{ij}:=(\partial_{x_j}u_i+\partial_{x_i}u_j)/2$, $\sigma:=-pI+2\eta D(u)$, and rowwise $(\operatorname{div}\sigma)_i:=\sum_j\partial_{x_j}\sigma_{ij}$. Put $I=(0,T)$. In case (B), put $B=\Omega$ and assume $\chi\in C^2(I\times B;\mathbb R^3)$, with each $\chi_t:B\to B$ an orientation-preserving $C^2$ diffeomorphism, and $u(t,\chi(t,a))=\partial_t\chi(t,a)$. In case (P), put $\widetilde\Omega=\mathbb R\times(0,h)\times\mathbb R$ and $\Lambda=\{(mL_x,0,nL_z):m,n\in\mathbb Z\}$; denote periodic lifts of $u,b,\sigma$ by $\widetilde u,\widetilde b,\widetilde\sigma$. Assume $\widetilde\chi\in C^2(I\times\widetilde\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$, with each $\widetilde\chi_t:\widetilde\Omega\to\widetilde\Omega$ an orientation-preserving $C^2$ diffeomorphism satisfying $\widetilde\chi(t,a+\lambda)=\widetilde\chi(t,a)+\lambda$ for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$, and $\widetilde u(t,\widetilde\chi(t,a))=\partial_t\widetilde\chi(t,a)$. For the material balance, write $(B,\chi,u^\sharp,b^\sharp,\sigma^\sharp)=(\Omega,\chi,u,b,\sigma)$ in case (B), and $(B,\chi,u^\sharp,b^\sharp,\sigma^\sharp)=(\widetilde\Omega,\widetilde\chi,\widetilde u,\widetilde b,\widetilde\sigma)$ in case (P). Here $\nu$ denotes the outward unit normal of $\chi_t(V)$; in case (P), the material-region integrals are on the Euclidean covering space. For every $t\in I$ and every nonempty bounded open $V\Subset B$ with $C^1$ boundary, assume the adopted material linear-momentum balance

$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\chi_t(V)}\rho u^\sharp\,dx=\int_{\chi_t(V)}\rho b^\sharp\,dx+\int_{\partial\chi_t(V)}\sigma^\sharp\nu\,dS,$$

Assume incompressibility as a model constraint, $\operatorname{div}u=0$ throughout the fluid domain (and $\operatorname{div}\widetilde u=0$ on its lift in case (P)). At every time impose one of the following wall laws: (N) no-slip, $u=g$ on $\Gamma$ for a prescribed tangential wall-velocity field $g\in C^1([0,T];C^2(\Gamma;\mathbb R^3))$ in metres per second with $g\cdot n=0$; or (S) stationary Navier friction on branch (B) only, $u\cdot n=0$ and $(\sigma n)_\tau=-\beta u_\tau$ on $\Gamma$, where $a_\tau:=a-(a\cdot n)n$ and $\beta\ge0$ is the adopted constant wall coefficient in pascal-seconds per metre. Then the local momentum equation

$$\rho\bigl(\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u\bigr)=\operatorname{div}\sigma+\rho b$$

holds on the fluid domain by the local momentum result from the adopted material balance; incompressibility is the separate model constraint stated above, not a conclusion of that result. Let $K(t):=\int_\Omega \rho|u(t,x)|^2/2\,dx$. Then for every $t\in(0,T)$ in case (N),

$$\frac{dK}{dt}=\int_\Omega \rho b\cdot u\,dx-2\eta\int_\Omega |D(u)|^2\,dx+\int_{\Gamma}g\cdot\sigma n\,dS,$$

and for every $t\in(0,T)$ in case (S),

$$\frac{dK}{dt}=\int_\Omega \rho b\cdot u\,dx-2\eta\int_\Omega |D(u)|^2\,dx-\beta\int_{\Gamma}|u_\tau|^2\,dS.$$

Every term has units of watts. In branch (B) only, in either stationary homogeneous case, (N) with $g=0$ or (S) with a fixed $\beta$, there is at most one solution in this smooth class for a given body force and initial velocity. These are deductions conditional on the stated model and wall assumptions; no solution-existence or empirical-applicability claim is made.

$$\rho\bigl(\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u\bigr)=\operatorname{div}\sigma+\rho b$$

Example.before:
Assume Countable Choice, meaning every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Let $L_x,L_z,h>0$ be lengths in metres and let $\Omega=(\mathbb R/L_x\mathbb Z)\times(0,h)\times(\mathbb R/L_z\mathbb Z)$ have periodic streamwise coordinate $x$ and spanwise coordinate $z$, with stationary walls $y=0,h$; all three coordinates are measured in metres. Let $\rho>0$ be constant density in kilograms per cubic metre, $\eta>0$ constant dynamic viscosity in pascal-seconds, and $p_0$ a constant pressure in pascals. Use the incompressible Newtonian model $\rho(\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u)=\operatorname{div}\sigma+\rho b$, $\operatorname{div}u=0$, $\sigma=-pI+2\eta D(u)$, where $D(u)_{ij}=(\partial_j u_i+\partial_i u_j)/2$ and divergence is rowwise. In the Poiseuille case let $G>0$ be a pressure-gradient scale in pascals per metre, set the body acceleration $b=(G/\rho,0,0)$ in metres per second squared and $p=p_0$, and define

$$u_P(x,y,z)=\left(\frac{G\,y(h-y)}{2\eta},0,0\right).$$

In the Couette case let $V\in\mathbb R$ be a tangential wall speed in metres per second, set $b=0$, $p=p_0$, and define

$$u_C(x,y,z)=\left(\frac{Vy}{h},0,0\right),$$

with no-slip wall velocity $g=0$ at $y=0$ and $g=(V,0,0)$ at $y=h$. Both fields are exact steady smooth solutions with impermeable no-slip walls. Their volumetric fluxes per unit span are $Q_P=Gh^3/(12\eta)$ and $Q_C=Vh/2$, each in square metres per second, and their vorticities $\omega:=\nabla\times u$ in inverse seconds are $\omega_P=(0,0,-G(h-2y)/(2\eta))$ and $\omega_C=(0,0,-V/h)$. In the Poiseuille case the body-force power per unit wall area equals viscous dissipation and stationary walls do no work. In the Couette case the moving top wall supplies power equal to viscous dissipation. A periodic pressure cannot contain the nonperiodic term $-Gx$; the stated constant pressure and body acceleration are the periodic-cell formulation. These are conditional predictions of the adopted equations, not observations or claims about all fluids.

Verification.before:
**Given:** The fields and model assumptions in the Example.

1.1 Let $\widetilde\Omega=\mathbb R\times(0,h)\times\mathbb R$ and $\Lambda=\{(mL_x,0,nL_z):m,n\in\mathbb Z\}$. For $U=U_P$ in the Poiseuille case and $U=U_C$ in the Couette case, define the lifted material map for each $t$ by $\widetilde\chi^U_t(x,y,z)=(x+tU(y),y,z)$. Both profiles are smooth, so this map is $C^\infty$; its inverse is $(x-tU(y),y,z)$. It maps $\widetilde\Omega$ onto itself, fixes the $y$ coordinate, and obeys $\widetilde\chi^U_t(a+\lambda)=\widetilde\chi^U_t(a)+\lambda$ for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$. Its Jacobian matrix is $\begin{pmatrix}1&tU'(y)&0\\0&1&0\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}$, with determinant $1>0$. Since $y$ is unchanged, $\partial_t\widetilde\chi^U_t=(U(y),0,0)=\widetilde u(t,\widetilde\chi^U_t(x,y,z))$, so each map descends to the periodic channel and has the example's velocity as its Eulerian velocity. Thus both profiles meet the material-motion hypothesis of [F1]. [given, F1, construct, algebra]

1.2 For either profile $u=(U(y),0,0)$, $\operatorname{div}u=0$, $\partial_tu=0$ and $(u\cdot\nabla)u=U(y)\partial_xu=0$. The only nonzero entries of $D$ are $D_{xy}=D_{yx}=U'/2$, so the only nonzero viscous shear entries are $\sigma_{xy}=\sigma_{yx}=\eta U'$, and $(\operatorname{div}\sigma)_x=-\partial_xp+\eta U''$. [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 In the Poiseuille case, $U_P(0)=U_P(h)=0$ and $U_P''=-G/\eta$. Thus $(\operatorname{div}\sigma)_x+\rho b_x=\eta U_P''+G=0$, and the other momentum components vanish, proving the steady equations and no-slip compatibility. Direct integration gives $Q_P=\int_0^hU_P(y)\,dy=Gh^3/(12\eta)$ and $\omega_{P,z}=-U_P'=-G(h-2y)/(2\eta)$. [given, F1, step 1.2, algebra]

2.2 In the Couette case, $U_C(0)=0$, $U_C(h)=V$, and $U_C''=0$, so the momentum equation holds with constant pressure and no body force; the velocity traces equal the stated wall velocities. Direct integration gives $Q_C=\int_0^hU_C(y)\,dy=Vh/2$ and $\omega_{C,z}=-U_C'=-V/h$. [given, F1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 For either profile, $|D|^2=(U')^2/2$, hence viscous dissipation per unit streamwise/spanwise wall area is $\eta\int_0^h(U')^2\,dy$. In the Poiseuille case this is $\frac{G^2}{4\eta}\int_0^h(h-2y)^2\,dy=G^2h^3/(12\eta)$, while body-force power is $\int_0^h\rho(G/\rho)U_P\,dy=GQ_P=G^2h^3/(12\eta)$; stationary-wall power is zero. This agrees with the stationary no-slip case of [F1]. [given, A1, F1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 In the Couette case viscous dissipation per unit wall area is $\eta\int_0^h(V/h)^2\,dy=\eta V^2/h$. At the top wall $n=(0,1,0)$ and $\sigma n$ has tangential component $\eta(V/h)(1,0,0)$, so wall power per unit area is $g\cdot\sigma n=\eta V^2/h$; the lower wall has $g=0$. This agrees with the tangential no-slip case of [F1]. Finally, a purported periodic pressure $p_0-Gx$ changes by $-GL_x$ under $x\mapsto x+L_x$, so it is not single-valued on $\Omega$ when $G>0$; the body-force formulation in the Example avoids that incompatibility. [given, A1, F1, step 2.2, algebra] ∎
